$comment: The pieces CLPR is made of, as the Architecture map and the "where it lives" sections show them. Text is rendered as written; refs are pinned links (see docs/provenance.md). Positions on the map stay in Architecture.astro: a new component needs a row here and a place in that SVG.

components.name: The specification
components.plain: The rulebook every other piece must follow. Two documents: a design document that explains the why (trust model, layers, roles, recovery) and a protocol specification that fixes the what (wire formats, state, algorithms, a pseudo-API). Alongside them, one folder per supported proof system saying exactly how that ledger's proofs are built and checked, and the decision records that explain the main changes made to the text.
components.detail: clpr-service.md (design), clpr-service-spec.md (normative: protobufs, on-ledger state model, verifier interface, §4 algorithms, §6 pseudo-API), verifiers/{hiero,qbft}/ (state_proof.md, verifier_contract.md, trust_anchor.md), ADR/ (five decision records, the newest in the final form the ADR guide defines) and clpr-options-to-consider.md (thirteen undecided items). The repository's LICENSE file is Apache-2.0; under the Labs charter, specifications are to be developed pursuant to the Community Specification License 1.0.

components.name: CLPR Service, native (Hiero)
components.plain: On Hiero networks the CLPR Service is built into the node software itself. Its queues and channels live in the node's own state tree, which is what makes them provable with the network's own signature. Contracts reach it through a fixed system address.
components.detail: Reachable from the EVM at system address 0x…016e. State in the Merkle tree → provable via Hiero state proofs (Channel leaf tag 482, ClprMessageValue leaf tag 498). The implementation lives in hiero-ledger/hiero-consensus-node.

components.name: CLPR Service, contract (EVM)
components.plain: On EVM ledgers the CLPR Service is a set of Solidity contracts. One immutable front door holds all the state and forwards each call to a module that knows how to handle it: channels, messaging, bundles, connectors, administration. Built and tested with Foundry.
components.detail: ClprService.sol is a DELEGATECALL router over ClprServiceStorage.sol; logic modules ChannelLogic, MessagingLogic, BundleLogic, ConnectorLogic, AdminLogic; state-mutating libraries BundleLib, ConnectorLib, ManifestLib; pure codecs ClprProtobuf*, ClprTypes. Read functions are not `view` (call via eth_call). storage-layout.json is a CI-checked snapshot because endpoints derive proof slots from it. Deploy through the viem CLI; clprEnabled stays false until explicitly enabled. Known divergences from the spec are listed in docs/bundle-flow.md and docs/quirks.md.

components.name: Verifier contracts
components.plain: The specialists that check another ledger's proofs. Each channel names one when it is created and keeps that address for life, though the contract behind it may be upgradeable. Two have verifier specifications in the specification repository: one for Hiero networks (checking the network's joint threshold signature) and one for EVM ledgers running QBFT (checking validator seals on block headers plus storage proofs). The repository also carries verifier code for other consensus families.
components.detail: hiero/HieroVerifier.sol (decodes the StateProof protobuf, derives the SHA-384 block root, calls TSSVerifier.sol for the hinTS BLS12-381 aggregate signature using EIP-2537 precompiles, walks leaf paths) with wraps/ helpers (WRAPS verification key, Poseidon/BN254); evm/qbft/QBFTVerifier.sol (committed seals, EIP-1186 account and storage proofs, epoch headers for rotation); evm/ethereum/EthMainnetVerifier.sol (sync-committee BLS light client); evm/sei/SeiCometBftVerifier.sol (CometBFT, Ed25519); evm/avalanche/MockAvalancheVerifier.sol. The spec's verifier documents describe a native verification path at 0x16e on Hiero.

components.name: Endpoint (relay) for EVM ledgers
components.plain: The endpoint program for EVM ledgers. It watches its own ledger's CLPR Service, talks to endpoints on the other side over gRPC, builds proofs of what its ledger has queued, dry-runs every bundle it receives, and submits the good ones as ordinary transactions. Its keys pay its own transaction fees and identify it to other endpoints over mutual TLS when the operator enables it; none of them can make a ledger accept a message.
components.detail: Java 25, Gradle, seven modules: proto (protobuf/PBJ), core (interfaces: TransactionSubmitter, ContractStateReader, BundlePayloadCodec, BundleConstructor, PeerSyncClient, PeerEndpointCache, CommitmentLevel), evm (JSON-RPC, ABI codec, ECDSA signer, EIP-1559 submission), grpc-server (Helidon + PBJ), grpc-client, sync (per-channel virtual-thread loops, peer selection: random, weighted by past successes; failing peers back off), app (YAML config, wiring, Prometheus metrics). Two listeners: info (9546, plaintext) and sync (9545, optional mandatory mTLS). Local proof types QBFT and CometBFT; Hiero only as a peer. Dockerfile and a Helm chart are included. Polls the chain rather than subscribing to events.

components.name: Endpoints on Hiero
components.plain: On a Hiero network there is no separate endpoint program: every consensus node is automatically an endpoint, and the list of them is kept up to date by the network itself. The node builds and signs the proofs as part of producing blocks; the endpoint only fetches the finished proof and carries it.
components.detail: The endpoint manifest is derived from the consensus roster (joins, leaves and identity rotations bump its version; stake-only changes do not). Proofs are built by the node's state-proof machinery and retrieved by the endpoint; the relay's HieroProofCodec parses them and submits them untrimmed. Misbehaving nodes are removed by Hiero governance, which removes them from the manifest.

components.name: The sync protocol
components.plain: How two endpoints talk: specified to run over mutual TLS, each sync is one stream for one channel, on which each side says how far it has got and receives the next messages after that point, up to the bundle limits, together with the proof. Requests are cheap and unproven; bundles are proven. Nothing is delivered that the receiver did not ask for.
components.detail: gRPC ClprEndpointService.sync: a bidirectional stream of ClprSyncPayload (channel_id, optional BundleRequest, optional BundleResponse); one stream is one cycle; both fields absent closes it. mTLS with an on-chain ECDSA P-384 CA per endpoint (≤ 512 bytes) and a per-process Ed25519 leaf. Message sizes bounded by max_sync_bytes. The reference endpoint still implements the earlier unary exchange: one ClprSyncPayload (channel_id, bundle_payload) each way, defined in clpr-relay-proto and served by clpr-relay-grpc-server.

components.name: Connector contracts
components.plain: The account that pays, present on both ledgers under one identity. On the sending side its contract decides whether to approve a message; on the receiving side its balance pays for running the message and its locked stake is what gets fined if it breaks its promise. Anyone can register one, on any channel, with a balance and a stake.
components.detail: IClprConnector: authorizeOutboundMessage(channelId, targetApplication, sender, messageData) → bool; payForExecution(amount) must transfer exactly amount to the caller; onInboundMessage(...) is a best-effort notification under a gas stipend. Registered by commit-reveal with connector_id = keccak256(channel_id ‖ public_key ‖ salt). EVM specifics: per-connector queue quota and geometric slashing (docs/evm-platform-spec.md).

components.name: Applications
components.plain: Your program. It calls one function to send and implements two callbacks to receive: one for an incoming message (whatever it returns becomes the reply) and one for the reply to a message it sent. It chooses, and should vet, the channel and the connector for each message; proofs, endpoints, verification and payment are handled below it.
components.detail: IClprApplication.onClprMessage(channelId, sender, messageData) → responseData; onClprResponse(channelId, messageId, status, responseData), invoked best-effort and only for senders with code. Send with IClprService.sendMessage(channelId, connectorId, targetApplication, messageData) → messageId. The repository's E2EApplication.sol shows a contract acting as both sender and receiver.

components.name: The lab: LF Decentralized Trust
components.plain: Where the specification, the smart contracts and the EVM endpoint are governed: an incubation space under the Linux Foundation's LF Decentralized Trust, offered by the Hedera Governing Council and open to anyone under the Apache License 2.0 with a Developer Certificate of Origin sign-off on every contribution.
components.detail: governance/: the signed Labs charter (TAC oversight; Apache-2.0 code; DCO; CSL-1.0 specifications; CC BY 4.0 docs), teams.yml (clpr-maintainers with maintain rights everywhere; lfdt-staff with admin on .github and governance) and CODEOWNERS. .github/profile/README.md: scope of the lab, terminology, the four layers, the extension process.
